assertionResults.reason: Init produced stack and LiteLLM configs with matching tier ports (8000/8001/8002), and `up --dry-run` used the same tier ports plus LiteLLM port 4000 exactly as configured.

Config propagation was confirmed for `litellm-port` (up/status on 5000), `memory-budget-pct` (recommend/init budget 76.8 GB), and `model-dir` (models command used custom directory), but validation of `default-quant -> pull` and `model-dir -> pull` could not be completed because `mlx-stack pull` is currently a placeholder (`Not yet implemented`).

With an induced fast-tier failure, up completed with mixed states (fast failed/down, other tiers + LiteLLM healthy), `down` cleaned all PID files including stale orphan PID, and a subsequent clean up run restored all tiers to healthy.

After externally crashing fast tier, status reported fast as crashed; rerunning `up` without `down` cleaned stale PID state and restarted only fast (new PID), while standard/longctx/LiteLLM remained already-running and unchanged.

In isolated auto-install mode, first `up` installed both dependencies (`Installing vllm-mlx...`, `Installing litellm...`) then started healthy services; after `down`, second `up` started services without reinstall messages.

Profile/recommend/init flow, schema_version rejection, and `vllm_flags -> up --dry-run` translation were validated, but full cross-command data consistency could not be completed because `bench --save` and `pull` are placeholder commands and do not create benchmark/models inventory artifacts required by the assertion.

With full stack healthy, `down --tier fast` stopped only fast and status showed fast=stopped while others stayed healthy; LiteLLM chat request still returned 200 via fallback (`x_selected_model: longctx`), and `up --tier fast` restored fast to healthy.

Interrupted `up` exited on SIGINT, then a rerun proceeded without lock conflict, reported stale PID cleanup, treated surviving services as already-running, restarted missing fast tier, and ended with all services healthy.
